headline: Tombaugh found a ninth planet, Gandhi walked to the sea, and the Nazis won a hundred and seven seats
texture: Clyde Tombaugh confirmed a ninth planet on February 18, working from photographs taken in January, and it was named Pluto. Gandhi set off on March 12 with seventy-eight followers to walk two hundred miles to the coast, and in April he broke the salt laws by picking up a handful of it. The National Socialists took a hundred and seven seats in the German federal election on September 14, up from a dozen.

Hoover signed the Smoot-Hawley Tariff on June 17, raising duties on more than twenty thousand goods while economists begged him not to. The studios instituted the Motion Picture Production Code on March 31 and then spent four years mostly ignoring it. Uruguay hosted and won the first World Cup, beating Argentina four to two in the final on July 30.

The year's second-biggest picture was Check and Double Check, built around the radio act Amos 'n' Andy and played by two white performers in blackface. Whoopee! outsold it and All Quiet on the Western Front came third, then won Best Picture. William Howard Taft died in March, the only man to have been both president and chief justice, and D. H. Lawrence died the same month.
